why: B reveals each intercept token as it is said, its margin note states the rule ('Asymptote: inside equals zero') instead of a bare label, its trap is two full sentences, and its last beat finishes the working ('two minus X is one'); A's trap is clipped fragments and its y-intercept line appears before it is said.
notes: Scores are for the pick with fixed_beats applied (assemble.mjs swaps them in).
Beat 5 'It lives to the left of X equals two' gave no reason. Fixed: the reason ('The inside must be positive') moved into the step-three beat, so beat 5 is only the shape.

Step three says 'Draw that shape' but nothing is drawn — the board has no log curve yet (bible §3.6). The highlight on X = 2 is the best this board can do; a student may still wonder where the drawing is. Revisit when the live graph is built.
Beat 4 highlights the whole equation on 'Minus in front'; the minus is not its own token, so the gesture is broad but fine.
Session edit after the read: beat 6 says 'draw that shape on your paper' — the board cannot draw a log curve yet, so the student draws it.
